title: Delta safeguard switch for drift-triggered rollback
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduces a configurable delta-safeguard toggle and heuristics to auto-rollback model rollouts when cohort-level drift or metric delta thresholds are exceeded. No customer-facing breaking changes.
summary: Add a delta-based safeguard switch and drift heuristics to trigger controlled rollbacks during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts.
description:
Context: We observed several partial degradations during staged model rollouts where small but sustained metric deltas among specific cohorts (latency, loss, token-error-rate) progressively violated SLAs before manual intervention could fully mitigate impact. This PR adds a 'delta safeguard' — a feature flag + lightweight evaluation layer that watches cohort deltas and enforces a stop-and-rollback when configured thresholds are breached.

Motivation: Existing rollout controllers support percentage-based gates and multi-metric gates, but they lack a concise mechanism to reason about directional delta (current vs baseline) for cohort slices and automatically perform a safe rollback without operator intervention. The delta safeguard is intended to be low-latency, explainable, and reversible.

What this PR changes: - Introduces pkg/safeguards/delta_switch.go: engine that computes per-cohort deltas against pinned baseline snapshots and exposes a compact decision API to the rollout controller. - Adds lightweight cohort snapshot persistence (sqlite-backed in test/dev, KVS integration hook for production) and a periodic reconciliation loop. - Extends services/rollout/controller.go to call the delta safeguard as an additional gate during canary, A/B, and shadow phases. - Adds a soft-stop path: on first breach, rollout pauses, emits a detailed event and trace span, and runs a secondary validation window (configurable grace period) before executing rollback. - Implements an emergency fast-rollback path when deltas exceed a hard-limit threshold. - Adds end-to-end tests in tests/integration/drift_rollback_test.go that simulate gradual drift and sudden regressions. - Adds runbook docs at docs/runbooks/drift-rollback.md and small Console UI affordance to display delta reasons at the rollout details page.

Design notes and constraints: - Delta computation is intentionally simple (percentage and absolute delta with smoothing) to avoid flakiness; we purposefully avoid complex ML detectors in this first iteration. - The safeguard exposes per-metric advisory scores (0..1) and a combined decision: continue/pause/rollback. Teams can opt-in per-environment via feature flag and tune thresholds per-cohort. - Persistence: production runtime uses the platform KVS; this PR includes an adapter interface so operators can provide etcd/consul/redis-backed stores.

Checklist: - [x] Core delta engine + API - [x] Controller integration (pause + rollback hooks) - [x] E2E tests for soft-stop and hard rollback - [x] Runbook and Console visibility - [x] Feature flag gating and defaults set to off for all tenants - [x] CI green (unit + integration)

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for delta math and smoothing rules. - Integration test simulates a canary where cohort A gradually drifts beyond soft_threshold: controller pauses, waits 60s grace, then marks canary unhealthy and rolls back. - Load smoke run to validate that the delta layer adds <1% CPU cost on the controller under 1000 rps. - Manual validation run on staging with feature flag enabled for a single tenant.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag off by default. 2) Canary enable for platform-internal tenants for 48h. 3) Enable for customer staging environments for 72h with monitoring dashboards. 4) Open opt-in for customer teams via Console toggle. 5) Evaluate metrics and enable by default if no regressions in 2 weeks.

Related work: This complements ENG-2199 (cohort similarity routing) by giving a reactive safety layer and ties to SUP-881 for the customer-reported drift incident in Jan. Docs: docs/runbooks/drift-rollback.md.

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on decision boundaries in delta_switch.go and the reconciliation window semantics in controller.go; both are intentionally conservative. Also please check the adapter interface for persistence for any obvious race conditions.
